00_COLLECTION.md.title: A modular receptor–reporter architecture for exploring cellular odor sensing
00_COLLECTION.md.body_markdown:
The collection contains **25 parts**: ten tuning-receptor CDSs, ten corresponding OR-IRES-mCherry modules, one GCaMP6f–Orco fusion and its four components. It allows another team to evaluate a related fluorescence system while seeing which evidence is available and which claims remain untested.

Insect tuning receptors and Orco form heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels [1]. This motivates co-expressing a tuning-receptor module with the shared reporter fusion. The design separates an interchangeable receptor sequence from a common reporter architecture; it does not establish equivalent expression, localization or sensing performance after each substitution.

| Design choice | Intended role | Evidence boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Human codon-adapted receptor DNA | Support mammalian expression | Team synthesis records; no matched native-codon comparison |
| OR–IRES–mCherry | Express receptor and marker as separate proteins | Red fluorescence is not a receptor abundance or localization assay |
| GCaMP6f–linker–Orco | Couple a calcium indicator to the co-receptor | Exploratory fluorescence; no independent localization proof |
| GCCACC on composites | Provide a mammalian initiation context | Sequence feature, not a comparative translation assay |
| No promoter or polyadenylation element | Let the host vector supply transcriptional control | Assembly must preserve start, frame and termination |
| Basic and composite versions | Permit reuse at different assembly levels | Basic components were not independently characterized |

Team records describe synthesis by GenScript in a pcDNA3.1(+) context. Native reference protein and human codon adaptation describe intended design, not verification of every experimental plasmid. Individual CDS pages retain FlyBase gene/transcript identifiers, RefSeq accession and reference length. Component pages identify GCaMP6f, the synthetic linker and vector-derived RSET leader.

The stable-cell study of Zboray et al. is relevant prior art [2]. Its Orco was codon-optimized, whereas its tuning-receptor sequences were not; it should not be described as an entirely wild-type-DNA platform. Our transient cultures, expression arrangement and acquisition method differ. These data do not isolate an advantage from codon adaptation, linker length or IRES layout.

### How the parts are used together

A sensing condition combines one tuning-receptor module with the shared reporter–co-receptor fusion. The tuning receptor supplies the variable recognition component; the IRES-mCherry segment supplies a separate expression-associated marker. The fusion supplies the common calcium-sensitive optical readout. This separation lets a user replace the tuning receptor without redesigning the reporting construct, while testing whether the new combination actually expresses and responds.

![Example tuning-module design](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts/architecture-bba-26zagfk0.svg)

*Or7a illustrates the interchangeable OR-IRES-mCherry arrangement. It encodes two separate proteins. This is a design schematic, not a measurement of receptor localization or stoichiometry.*

![Shared reporter–co-receptor fusion design](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts/architecture-bba-26e11z80.svg)

*The RSET–GCaMP6f–(GGGGS)₃–DmOrco arrangement is shared by the ten sensing conditions. The four basic components allow the individual sequence elements to be reused; their separate presence in the collection does not mean they were independently tested.*

There are three distinct questions in the evidence below: was a labelled DNA preparation obtained; is localized reporter-associated fluorescence detectable in fixed cells; and how do later fluorescence changes compare with handling and biological-background controls? Success at one stage does not answer the next. The following records make the measured stage and the unresolved transition visible.

### Ligand panel and assembly

P2 includes VUAA1, six VOCs and a buffer-only row. VUAA1 is a literature-supported Orco agonist [3]. Zboray et al. used 2-heptanone as an Or85b reference compound. Their Or98a reference, 6-methyl-5-hepten-2-one, is absent from P2. DoOR 2.0 can inform ligand selection [4], but its normalized measurements are not quantitative predictions for this HEK293 assay. A complete receptor-specific rationale for the supplied panel is not documented.

All 25 identifiers were returned as **published** by the official Registry API on 19 October 2026. The index records lengths and a motif scan. Many sequences contain internal restriction sites; the collection is not uniformly compatible with a single restriction-based standard. A motif-free result alone does not certify compatibility: flanking sequence, overhang design, reading frame, vector and the standard also matter. This read-only review did not change Registry records.

00_COLLECTION.md.title: Evidence provenance, paired fluorescence measurements and control contrasts
00_COLLECTION.md.body_markdown:
### Construction and microscopy

The cloning record contains three colony photographs and four undigested plasmid gels. DNA is visible in **24 sample lanes**, two for each of **12 construct labels**, with similar migration within each pair. This supports DNA presence, not insert identity or restriction-fragment size. Uncut plasmid conformation affects migration. Colony growth identifies candidates for further checks, not successful assembly or sensor function.

The endpoint HEK293 image set contains **25 fields across 12 conditions**, with one to three fields per condition, around **44–48 h post-transfection**, before G418 selection, after **2% PFA fixation** and DAPI staining without documented permeabilization. Analysis pools eligible resolvable DAPI objects and reports RED-, GREEN- and dual-positive fractions at a blank-derived p99 cutoff; p95 and p99.5 sensitivity outputs are retained. Eligible objects cover only a subset of DAPI foreground. These fractions are not whole-culture transfection efficiency or viability; fields are not independent biological repeats. Image-to-P2 batch identity is unresolved.

### Construction evidence and condition map

The three original colony photographs cover ten tuning-receptor labels and two reporter/co-receptor-related labels. Photographs 1–3 and gels A–D are reused directly from the existing official image assets, without new image synthesis or selective lane reconstruction.

Across all four gels, the preserved processing is rigid orientation and contiguous cropping, without lane splicing or intensity adjustment. The source-manifest records original TIFF hashes and the lane map.*

### P2 preparation and acquisition

P2 is one HEK293 plate at approximately **72 h post-transfection**, without G418 selection. Columns 1–10 are Or7a, Or19a, Or42a, Or98a, Or22a, Or67a, Or67b, Or59b, Or85b and Or35a, each with the fusion. Column 11 is reporter fusion alone; column 12 is **untransfected cells**, not cell-free buffer. Each condition–stimulus combination has one well. Raw headers span **10–11 October 2026**; team confirmation on 11 October does not make this a one-day acquisition.

Confirmed buffer: **140 mM NaCl, 5 mM KCl, 2 mM CaCl₂, 1 mM MgCl₂, 5 mM HEPES-Na and 20 mM glucose, pH 7.3, 340 mOsm**. VUAA1 was prepared in DMSO; final solvent fraction is unknown. VOCs were initially supplied in aqueous solution and diluted in buffer, but stock and final molar concentrations are unresolved. Plain buffer is not a documented matched vehicle for VUAA1.

CSV exports verify **482 ± 8 nm excitation / 530 ± 20 nm emission**, five-point baseline runs and 15-point response runs at **12-second cycles**, with response timestamps **0–168 s**. Four stages define each stimulus row: F0a, blank, F0b and test. Each response is normalized to its paired baseline.

The report identifies a BMG CLARIOstar Plus, GREINER 96F bottom plate, bottom optics, LP504, −4.1 mm focal setting, 20 flashes, 0.5 s settling and enhanced dynamic range off. It describes 50 µL additions, taking volume from 100 to 150 to 200 µL, with an eight-channel pipette for columns 1–8 then 9–12. These are report-level details, not settings independently recovered from CSVs. Numeric gain, addition-to-read delay, actual temperature and extent of reported detachment are unresolved. Nominal final VUAA1 is **50 µM** in the report, not independently confirmed by stock-preparation records. These data do not support dose–response or EC₅₀ estimates.

### Calculation and exclusions

F0 is each well's five-point paired-baseline mean. The peak statistic is the largest mean of three consecutive response readings. With normalized changes ΔFblank and ΔFtest:

- **R(s,c) = ΔFtest(s,c) − ΔFblank(s,c).** Original ΔFcorr, retained as the base fluorescence difference.
- **B(s,c) = R(s,c) − R(H,c).** H is the separate buffer-only well in the same column/condition.
- **D(s,c) = B(s,c) − [R(s,12) − R(H,12)].** Column 12 is untransfected cells under the same stimulus; H12 is its buffer reference.

R is dimensionless: 0.10 is a difference of normalized changes, not a ten-percent cell fraction. B and D add different-well controls. Buffer-row B and D, and untransfected-column D, are zero algebraically. Shared reference wells make contrasts dependent.

Rows **B (ethyl propionate)** and **C (isopentyl acetate)** are excluded following reported gain changes. All 96 wells and quality flags remain archived: **72 retained, 24 excluded**. Numeric gain is unavailable, so “retained” means exploratory, not verified constant-gain acquisition. Figure omission or hatching does not reinstate exclusions.

Earlier thresholds, including a roughly **0.13448** three-SD heuristic from six untransfected retained rows, remain only in the historical audit. Those rows represent different stimuli, not independently repeated blanks. Current tables do not classify responses using this heuristic, a first-point fraction or the earlier multi-rule acceptance test. B and D do not create replication or resolve missing solvent controls.

### Reading the effect of each control

The same VUAA1 stimulus provides a compact comparison of all twelve columns. Reading R, then B, then D asks three different questions: how the second round differs from the first in one well; how that value compares with the same-condition buffer-only well; and how much remains after the equivalent untransfected-cell contrast.

![VUAA1 control dependence across all twelve conditions](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts/p2-vuaa1-control-dependence.svg)

*VUAA1 row A, one well per condition. The plot shows the computed R→B→D progression, without adding error bars or a significance threshold. Fusion-only A11 remains positive; Or35a changes sign after its large buffer reference is subtracted; Or67a and Or67b increase after subtraction of negative buffer references. The untransfected D value is zero by construction and is a control identity, not independent evidence of no response.*

This comparison makes the control dependence explicit. A control correction can increase, decrease or reverse an observed contrast; none of those operations identifies its biological cause. The full retained stimulus table above and the condition-specific part tables should be read alongside this single-stimulus overview.

A11 remains positive after both contrasts. A10 has positive R but negative B and D because its buffer reference H10 is larger. F01 remains positive after correction, yet its R partly reflects subtraction of a declining blank round. Selecting the largest value, or treating every negative contrast as a nonfunctional receptor, would be misleading. Part pages report every retained B and D per construct; the CSV retains all 96 wells.

![Paired-round examples and control dependence](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts/curve-collection-false-positives.avif)

*Selected traces compare first and second response runs. This is a diagnostic comparison, not classification of true or false responses. Time is relative to each exported run, not a precisely recorded addition.*

The combined record documents prepared plasmid samples, reporter-associated fluorescence in fixed cells, and exploratory changes in a later plate assay. These answer different questions. They do not together prove membrane-localized, receptor-specific detection without the missing identity, vehicle, calcium-dependence and replication controls.

00_COLLECTION.md.title: What another team can reuse and what must be validated next
00_COLLECTION.md.body_markdown:
The contribution is a modular design with traceable measurements and explicit controls. The evidence does not establish a validated sensor collection. Fourteen basic components were not tested independently; eleven composite conditions were not independently repeated. Pages and technical fields do not increase biological replication.

The consequential gaps are numeric gain, verified stimulus and vehicle preparation, experimental-plasmid identity, cell state and handling timing. Resolve these, then repeat a focused positive-control and ligand panel with independent cultures and matched controls. Assess expression, localization and calcium dependence separately. Reproducible responses should precede concentration-response modelling, specificity, stability or detection-limit claims.

R is sensitive to a first-round decrease, while B and D depend on additional wells. Neither calculation identifies the biological explanation. Complete traces, both rounds and controls are more informative than selecting the normalization producing the largest value.

### Practical reuse of the collection

| Starting point | What is supplied | What the next user needs to establish |
|---|---|---|
| One tuning CDS | Reference identifiers, submitted sequence length, assembly-site scan and matching module | Expression context and a suitable functional readout |
| OR-IRES-mCherry module | Bicistronic layout, marker-associated endpoint evidence and its condition-specific P2 values | Co-expression with the reporter fusion, localization and ligand/vehicle controls |
| Reporter–Orco fusion | Domain layout, fusion-only microscopy and VUAA1/control traces | Intact protein, calcium dependence and reproducibility in the chosen host |
| Analysis workflow | Original calculation code, methods, small characterization tables and traceable exclusions | Recorded inputs and fixed acquisition settings for any new dataset |

The collection is useful as a documented starting architecture and a worked example of control-sensitive fluorescence analysis. It is not yet a completed, validated multi-odor sensor. The part pages preserve the differences among conditions rather than treating the presence of 25 sequences as 25 successful functional tests.

### Reproducible team evidence

Analysis code and reusable documentation are published in the official iGEM GitLab repository. The three small derived characterization tables below accompany the documentation; they preserve the canonical values and quality flags. Original RFU exports, complete time-series data and microscopy TIFFs remain in the unpublished Zenodo preparation package. No Zenodo DOI or public raw-data download is claimed.

- [P2 well summary](https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/nthu/-/raw/main/docs/aerosense/parts/data/plate-p2-well-summary.csv): both round-level changes and all-well flags.
- [P2 control contrasts](https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/nthu/-/raw/main/docs/aerosense/parts/data/plate-p2-control-contrasts.csv): R, B, D and their reference wells, including excluded rows clearly flagged.
- [Microscopy condition counts](https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/nthu/-/raw/main/docs/aerosense/parts/data/nuclear-object-per-condition.csv): field counts, denominators and all three threshold settings.
- [Executed P2 methods](https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/nthu/-/raw/main/code/aerosense/wetlab/aerosense-wiki/assets/results/final-test/plate-p2-methods.html) and [P2 analysis code](https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/nthu/-/blob/main/code/aerosense/wetlab/aerosense-wiki/assets/results/final-test/analyze_plate_p2.py).
- [Microscopy analysis code](https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/nthu/-/blob/main/code/aerosense/wetlab/aerosense-wiki/assets/results/microscopy/analyze_nuclear_objects.py).
- The essential colony, gel, fixed-cell and plate-assay evidence is embedded in these documents. The official Wiki currently serves an earlier template; the expanded local Results page is not treated as a published data source here.

Canonical unpublished archive paths: `zenodo-release/aerosense-wiki/wetlab results/` (original measurements); `assets/results/final-test/derived/plate-p2-timeseries.csv` and `experiment-metadata.json` within the same archive; `assets/results/microscopy/nuclear-object-per-field.csv` and `source-manifest.json`. These are provenance paths, not live download links.

BBa_2629NIWH__Or19a-IRES-mCherry.md.title: Or19a expression module with an independent fluorescent marker
BBa_2629NIWH__Or19a-IRES-mCherry.md.body_markdown:
This module is intended to supply the tuning receptor in a co-expression system with GCaMP6f–Orco (`BBa_26E11Z80`). The receptor and co-receptor form the expected sensing complex; the IRES drives translation of mCherry as a separate protein. Red fluorescence is an expression-associated marker, not a measurement of receptor abundance, surface localization or channel function.

The receptor's design source is recorded on its CDS page. Team records describe human codon adaptation and GenScript synthesis in a pcDNA3.1(+) context. Neither enhanced expression from codon adaptation nor an optimal OR:Orco ratio has been established by a matched comparison.

### Functional architecture

![Or19a bicistronic architecture](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts/architecture-bba-2629niwh.svg)

*Design schematic, not to scale: the Or19a coding sequence is followed by EMCV IRES and mCherry. Or19a and mCherry are separate proteins; the GCaMP6f–Orco fusion is supplied by a separate co-expressed construct. Membrane localization and channel function are hypotheses to test, not observations established by the diagram.*

### Literature context

The stable-cell study of Zboray et al. included Or19a but did not obtain responses to its tested VOC panel. That result motivates checking the expression system and ligand selection separately.

The [collection](00_COLLECTION.md) records the tested ligand panel and its selection limits. This screen is not an exhaustive ligand profile for this receptor.

BBa_262WP16P__RSET-leader.md.body_markdown:
The published sequence is **105 bp**, encoding a 35-amino-acid N-terminal leader derived from the pRSET vector series. It includes a His-tag/Xpress-associated detection region and is placed before GCaMP6f in `BBa_26E11Z80`. The pRSET manual describes the parent vector's 6×His tag, T7 gene-10 leader, Xpress epitope and enterokinase site [1]; the actual assembled sequence should determine which residues and cleavage context are present.

### Intended use

The leader offers an antibody-based route to assess protein abundance and apparent molecular size, independently of calcium-dependent GCaMP brightness. A Western blot could help establish whether a full-length product is detectable. It would not, by itself, establish membrane localization or channel activity; these require other measurements.

The sequence is a synthetic vector-derived element. Its N-terminal position does not prove that it is biologically inert or incapable of affecting folding. No tagged-versus-untagged comparison has been performed.

### Functional architecture

![RSET leader within the reporter fusion](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts/architecture-bba-262wp16p.svg)

*Design context, not to scale. The 105 bp RSET leader is upstream of GCaMP6f and supplies the fusion translation start; it is a detection-handle design rather than a tested purification or localization element.*

### Reading this component within the tested fusion

The parent [BBa_26E11Z80](BBa_26E11Z80__GCaMP6f-GGGGS3-DmOrco.md) carries this leader ahead of the calcium indicator. Its construction, fixed-cell images and P2 traces describe the complete fusion. None measures anti-tag binding or cleavage, so the leader should be selected for its sequence-defined detection handle rather than an experimentally established improvement in this sensor.

For reuse, the key junction is the in-frame connection to GCaMP6f: this leader provides the upstream translation start that the submitted GCaMP6f fragment lacks. If the leader is removed, an appropriate replacement start context must be supplied. A tag-directed assay can answer whether an intact product is detected; calcium imaging answers a different question about the fluorescent reporter.

### Characterisation status

No anti-His or anti-Xpress blot, cleavage experiment or purification result is documented for this part. The parent fusion's exploratory fluorescence is not an isolated test of tag performance. Accordingly, no detection efficiency, cleavage efficiency or lack of functional interference is claimed.

The fusion is intended to report calcium changes in an Orco-containing sensing system. Insect odorant receptors have an intracellular N-terminus in the established topology [1], which motivates placing GCaMP6f on that side. A single ORF encodes one copy of each domain, but this does not guarantee intact mature protein, equal functional stoichiometry or plasma-membrane localization.

The related stable-cell architecture of Zboray et al. provides a design precedent [2]. Our linker is (GGGGS)₃, 15 amino acids, compared with their eight-amino-acid connector. Its intended flexibility is a design rationale; no side-by-side linker comparison establishes an advantage. The different host-expression arrangements and acquisition methods also prevent assigning differences between the two studies to linker length.

BBa_26E11Z80__GCaMP6f-GGGGS3-DmOrco.md.body_markdown:
### Endpoint microscopy

The image condition labelled “ORCO only” contains this reporter fusion without a tuning-receptor module. Across **three technical fields**, **342 eligible DAPI objects** were retained. At the blank-derived p99 threshold, **24/342 (7.0%)** were GREEN-positive, **0/342 (0.0%)** were RED-positive, and none were positive in both channels. Eligible objects represented **19.6%** of DAPI foreground. The absence of an mCherry module makes the red channel a useful control within this image set.

These fixed-cell measurements are localized reporter-associated fluorescence counts, not a whole-culture transfection efficiency or evidence of membrane localization. The blank yielded 1/170 objects above each threshold but also supplied the cutoff, so it is not an independent false-positive-rate estimate. BBa_26E11Z80__GCaMP6f-GGGGS3-DmOrco.md.body_markdown:
The A11 observation is consistent with a response worth testing further, but this experiment alone does not prove channel gating, extracellular-calcium dependence or plasma-membrane localization. VUAA1 activation of Orco is established in the literature [3]; that prior result supports the experimental hypothesis rather than substituting for controls on this fusion.

The Orco-only condition also shows positive D values for retained odorant rows, including **+0.1056 for 2-heptanone** and **+0.1298 for valeric acid**. Thus, a positive contrast in a tuning-receptor condition cannot automatically be assigned to that receptor. The 12-second sampling and unrecorded addition-to-read delays cannot distinguish all rapid optical, mechanical and biological explanations from curve shape alone. The peak time is an acquisition statistic, not a measured channel response time.

Comparison with a selected stable-cell line cannot identify the cause of a smaller or larger amplitude here: expression context, cell handling, stimulation and normalization differ. No stable clone, optimized linker, receptor specificity, calcium affinity or detection limit has been established for this construct.

The next informative evidence would combine verified plasmid identity and expression with fixed-gain repeated cultures, concentration-matched vehicle controls, Ca²⁺-dependence controls and an appropriate localization assay. BBa_26E21OEQ__GGGGSx3-linker.md.title: A synthetic 15-amino-acid linker for a reporter–receptor fusion
BBa_26E21OEQ__GGGGSx3-linker.md.body_markdown:
The published sequence is **45 bp**, encoding **(GGGGS)₃**, a 15-amino-acid glycine–serine linker. It is placed in frame between GCaMP6f and DmOrco in `BBa_26E11Z80`, without an intervening stop codon. Its purpose is to provide a flexible connection while retaining a single fusion protein.

### Design rationale

Zboray et al. used an eight-amino-acid Gly₂SerGly₃SerGly connector in their related reporter–Orco architecture [1]. The present construct uses a longer connector as a design choice intended to allow domain motion. No matched comparison establishes that 15 amino acids improves folding, expression, localization or signal over eight amino acids.

This is a synthetic sequence rather than a gene from an organism. The three peptide repeats use diversified synonymous codons. That sequence choice does not guarantee freedom from synthesis errors or instability; the assembled product should still be sequence-verified.

### Functional architecture

![Glycine–serine linker between reporter and receptor](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts/architecture-bba-26e21oeq.svg)

*Design context, not to scale. The highlighted 45 bp (GGGGS)₃ segment joins GCaMP6f to DmOrco in frame. It is an internal connector, not an independent protein or a measured improvement over another linker.*

### Junction-specific reuse

The linker makes the two domains a single translational product while allowing a flexible connection. Its two junctions, with the end of GCaMP6f and the start of DmOrco, are therefore the relevant sequence features for reuse. Preserve the reading frame and the intended domain order; changing the length, composition or attachment point creates a different fusion design.

The parent [BBa_26E11Z80](BBa_26E11Z80__GCaMP6f-GGGGS3-DmOrco.md) documents the assembly context, fixed-cell fluorescence and P2 measurements. They provide evidence about a construct containing this linker, but no comparison isolates the linker's contribution. A useful comparative study would keep the remaining fusion and expression context constant while comparing connector variants; no result from such a comparison is claimed here.

### Characterisation status

The linker was not isolated or tested across a length series. The exploratory P2 observations belong to the complete fusion and cannot establish the linker's optimum length or functional neutrality. Reuse should preserve the reading frame and test the behavior of the complete fusion in its intended host.

The published sequence is **1,461 bp**, including an ATG start and terminal stop codon, for a 486-amino-acid reference protein. Orco participates with tuning receptors in insect heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels [1]. Work in Drosophila also establishes a role in receptor localization and function [2]. These findings motivate co-expression with a tuning receptor, but they do not prove that our particular construct reaches the HEK293 plasma membrane.

VUAA1 can activate Orco-containing channels, including Orco without a tuning receptor, in published systems [3]. In this collection it is used as a functional probe, with the qualification that fluorescence changes require controls before being assigned to channel activation.

Use this bare CDS to choose your own reporter or expression arrangement. The provided composite `BBa_26E11Z80` joins GCaMP6f to the Orco N-terminus through a 15-amino-acid linker. Removing or relocating domains creates a different construct and requires a new characterization.

![DmOrco coding sequence within the shared sensing system](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts/architecture-bba-26lwikbq.svg)

The ORCO-labelled construction plate and paired gel A lanes 1–2 are preserved on the [fusion page](BBa_26E11Z80__GCaMP6f-GGGGS3-DmOrco.md). They are not reassigned as sequence confirmation of this basic part.

The later fusion-only condition is useful as a control for the ten tuning-receptor modules. Its retained D values include +0.1725 for VUAA1, +0.1056 for 2-heptanone and +0.1298 for valeric acid. Thus, positive fluorescence contrasts in the collection cannot automatically be attributed to the tuning receptor. The complete fusion and its cellular background must be considered. Reusing the bare Orco CDS without GCaMP6f requires a separate readout and a fresh characterization of that arrangement.

### Characterisation status

This untagged CDS was not tested separately. The P2 column labelled “ORCO only” contains the **GCaMP6f–Orco fusion without a tuning receptor**, not this naked CDS. Its microscopy and VUAA1-associated measurements belong to the composite. They cannot be reassigned as independent functional evidence for this basic part.

### Intended role and assembly

Insect tuning receptors and Orco form heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels [1]. This CDS supplies the Or59b subunit. For either design, supply suitable transcriptional control and polyadenylation from the mammalian vector, and verify start/stop codons and reading frame against the actual assembled sequence. Expression, localization and channel function require separate checks.

| Item | Team design record |
|---|---|
| Organism | *Drosophila melanogaster* |
| Gene | [FBgn0034865](https://flybase.org/reports/FBgn0034865.html) |
| Transcript | FBtr0072021 |
| RefSeq protein | [NP_523822](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/protein/NP_523822) |
| Reference protein length | 398 amino acids |
| Production | Human codon-adapted DNA, synthesised by GenScript; used in a pcDNA3.1(+) expression context |

Undigested gel migration and colony growth cannot verify this insert's identity. The submitted sequence and the experimental clone should be checked independently before reuse.

The corresponding [BBa_26Y7CI2H module](BBa_26Y7CI2H__Or59b-IRES-mCherry.md) places this coding sequence upstream of IRES-mCherry. This bare CDS was not tested separately. Its composite module page contains the condition-specific microscopy counts and exploratory P2 fluorescence measurements. Codon adaptation was chosen to support mammalian expression. BBa_26QHYP02__GCaMP6f.md.title: A calcium-dependent fluorescent domain for a translational fusion
BBa_26QHYP02__GCaMP6f.md.body_markdown:
GCaMP6f is a genetically encoded calcium indicator described by Chen et al. [1]. Calcium-dependent changes in the calmodulin–peptide/circularly permuted GFP architecture alter green fluorescence. The team design attributes the source to Addgene plasmid #40755 [2].

The published part sequence is **1,245 bp**. It starts with `GTG`, not an initiator `ATG`, and does not end with a stop codon; this submitted fragment is intended for an in-frame fusion context. In `BBa_26E11Z80`, an upstream RSET leader supplies the translation start and the downstream linker connects it to Orco. A standalone expression design needs a suitable start context, reading frame and termination sequence.

### Why this domain

The fast GCaMP6 variant offers a literature-supported starting point for following changing calcium signals. Its performance in neuronal studies does not specify the kinetics, sensitivity or dynamic range of this Orco fusion in HEK293 cells. Our manual-addition, 12-second sampling assay cannot independently resolve channel-opening kinetics or show that indicator speed is limiting.

GCaMP fluorescence is an intensity measurement. It can change with reporter abundance, cell number, optical conditions and the cellular environment as well as calcium. Therefore, changes in signal are not automatically receptor responses. Gain should be fixed and the measurement range checked experimentally; no universal baseline percentage or saturation margin is established here.

### Functional architecture

![GCaMP6f domain within the reporter fusion](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts/architecture-bba-26qhyp02.svg)

*Design context, not to scale. The highlighted 1,245 bp domain begins with GTG and has no terminal stop codon. The parent fusion supplies its translation start upstream and continues through the linker into Orco; this is not a standalone complete expression cassette.*

### Reading the reporter-associated evidence

The parent [BBa_26E11Z80](BBa_26E11Z80__GCaMP6f-GGGGS3-DmOrco.md) supplies the relevant fixed-cell and kinetic observations. In its fusion-only image condition, 24/342 eligible objects were GREEN-positive at the blank-derived p99 cutoff, compared with 1/170 in the blank that also defined the cutoff. The P2 VUAA1 well A11 has R = +0.2148, B = +0.2316 and D = +0.1725. These are observations on the complete reporter–receptor construct, not calibration of free GCaMP6f.

The useful distinction for reuse is between having measurable green fluorescence and having a calibrated calcium indicator in a new context. The first is supported by the parent condition. The second would require an independent calibration of the chosen expression arrangement; these data do not determine a calcium concentration, affinity or dynamic range.

### Characterisation status

The free indicator was not measured independently. Endpoint microscopy and P2 measurements were made on constructs containing the domain and are reported on the parent fusion page. They do not determine this basic part's calcium affinity, pH response, dynamic range, maturation efficiency or performance relative to other GCaMP variants.

BBa_26UHN7NT__Or42a-CDS.md.body_markdown:
### Intended role and assembly

Insect tuning receptors and Orco form heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels [1]. This CDS supplies the Or42a subunit. For this platform it is co-expressed with the GCaMP6f–Orco fusion `BBa_26E11Z80`; a response depends on the assembled system and the cellular context. The isolated sequence is not a complete sensing device.

Use this part to choose your own promoter, expression marker or fusion arrangement. The corresponding bicistronic module includes a GCCACC initiation context and IRES-mCherry. For either design, supply suitable transcriptional control and polyadenylation from the mammalian vector, and verify start/stop codons and reading frame against the actual assembled sequence. Expression, localization and channel function require separate checks.

### Functional architecture

![Or42a CDS in the expression-module context](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts/architecture-bba-26uhn7nt.svg)

*Design context, not to scale. The highlighted Or42a CDS is the basic part; GCCACC initiation context, EMCV IRES and mCherry belong to the assembled expression module, not this isolated sequence. The calcium-reporter/Orco construct is a separate partner. The diagram does not assert experimental localization or activity.*

### Sequence provenance

| Item | Team design record |
|---|---|
| Organism | *Drosophila melanogaster* |
| Gene | [FBgn0033041](https://flybase.org/reports/FBgn0033041.html) |
| Transcript | FBtr0086052 |
| RefSeq protein | [NP_523622](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/protein/NP_523622) |
| Reference protein length | 406 amino acids |
| Production | Human codon-adapted DNA, synthesised by GenScript; used in a pcDNA3.1(+) expression context |

The intended protein is the native reference receptor; codon adaptation concerns the DNA design. These identifiers establish the design source, not sequence confirmation of every laboratory plasmid. Undigested gel migration and colony growth cannot verify this insert's identity. The submitted sequence and the experimental clone should be checked independently before reuse.

### Trace from this CDS to the tested condition

The corresponding [BBa_26Q1Q094 module](BBa_26Q1Q094__Or42a-IRES-mCherry.md) places this coding sequence upstream of IRES-mCherry. Its documentation shows the Or42a-labelled colony plate (photograph 2, lower-right), gel D lanes 7–8, the fixed-cell **Or42a+ORCO** condition and P2 **column 03**. These labels connect the design to the team's preparation records. They do not resolve which saved colony supplied each later assay or independently confirm the DNA sequence.

A user can therefore reuse the CDS design and inspect the module-level observations, while choosing a different transcriptional or reporter arrangement. Such a change should be characterized as a new expression context; neither mCherry brightness nor the fusion's calcium-associated fluorescence measures the abundance or activity of this isolated receptor protein.

### Evidence and limits

This bare CDS was not tested separately. Its composite module page contains the condition-specific microscopy counts and exploratory P2 fluorescence measurements. Those observations must not be counted again as an independent characterisation of this basic part, nor taken as proof of membrane localization or receptor specificity.

Codon adaptation was chosen to support mammalian expression. The stable-cell study by Zboray et al. provides relevant precedent [2], but the present records do not contain a matched wild-type-versus-adapted comparison. No improvement in expression or sensing can therefore be attributed to codon adaptation here.

The published CDS includes an ATG start and terminal stop codon. Its promoter, initiation context and polyadenylation must be supplied appropriately for the intended expression system.

### Intended role and assembly

Insect tuning receptors and Orco form heteromeric ligand-gated ion channels [1]. This CDS supplies the Or67a subunit. For this platform it is co-expressed with the GCaMP6f–Orco fusion `BBa_26E11Z80`; a response depends on the assembled system and the cellular context. The isolated sequence is not a complete sensing device.

Use this part to choose your own promoter, expression marker or fusion arrangement. The corresponding bicistronic module includes a GCCACC initiation context and IRES-mCherry. For either design, supply suitable transcriptional control and polyadenylation from the mammalian vector, and verify start/stop codons and reading frame against the actual assembled sequence. Expression, localization and channel function require separate checks.

### Functional architecture

![Or67a CDS in the expression-module context](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/parts/architecture-bba-26xxp4k7.svg)

*Design context, not to scale. The highlighted Or67a CDS is the basic part; GCCACC initiation context, EMCV IRES and mCherry belong to the assembled expression module, not this isolated sequence. The calcium-reporter/Orco construct is a separate partner. The diagram does not assert experimental localization or activity.*

### Sequence provenance

| Item | Team design record |
|---|---|
| Organism | *Drosophila melanogaster* |
| Gene | [FBgn0036009](https://flybase.org/reports/FBgn0036009.html) |
| Transcript | FBtr0076375 |
| RefSeq protein | [NP_524005](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/protein/NP_524005) |
| Reference protein length | 407 amino acids |
| Production | Human codon-adapted DNA, synthesised by GenScript; used in a pcDNA3.1(+) expression context |

The intended protein is the native reference receptor; codon adaptation concerns the DNA design. These identifiers establish the design source, not sequence confirmation of every laboratory plasmid. Undigested gel migration and colony growth cannot verify this insert's identity. The submitted sequence and the experimental clone should be checked independently before reuse.

### Trace from this CDS to the tested condition

The corresponding [BBa_265G8CE1 module](BBa_265G8CE1__Or67a-IRES-mCherry.md) places this coding sequence upstream of IRES-mCherry. Its documentation shows the Or67a-labelled colony plate (photograph 2, upper-left), gel D lanes 3–4, the fixed-cell **Or67a+ORCO** condition and P2 **column 06**. These labels connect the design to the team's preparation records. They do not resolve which saved colony supplied each later assay or independently confirm the DNA sequence.

A user can therefore reuse the CDS design and inspect the module-level observations, while choosing a different transcriptional or reporter arrangement. Such a change should be characterized as a new expression context; neither mCherry brightness nor the fusion's calcium-associated fluorescence measures the abundance or activity of this isolated receptor protein.

### Evidence and limits

This bare CDS was not tested separately. Its composite module page contains the condition-specific microscopy counts and exploratory P2 fluorescence measurements. Those observations must not be counted again as an independent characterisation of this basic part, nor taken as proof of membrane localization or receptor specificity.

Codon adaptation was chosen to support mammalian expression. The stable-cell study by Zboray et al. provides relevant precedent [2], but the present records do not contain a matched wild-type-versus-adapted comparison. No improvement in expression or sensing can therefore be attributed to codon adaptation here.

The published CDS includes an ATG start and terminal stop codon. Its promoter, initiation context and polyadenylation must be supplied appropriately for the intended expression system.

The stable-cell study of Zboray et al. included Or7a but did not obtain responses to its tested VOC panel. That result is specific to their system; it does not establish a universal absence of Or7a ligand responses.

The [collection](00_COLLECTION.md) records the tested ligand panel and its selection limits. This screen is not an exhaustive ligand profile for this receptor.

### Endpoint microscopy

The fixed HEK293 image set contains **2 technical fields** labelled Or7a+ORCO, with **192 eligible DAPI objects**. At the blank-derived p99 cutoff, RED-positive objects were **21/192 (10.9%)**, GREEN-positive **3/192 (1.6%)**, and both-positive **1/192 (0.5%)**. Eligible objects represented 16.2% of DAPI foreground.

These are counts around resolvable nuclear objects, not whole-culture transfection efficiency or viability. The images were acquired around 44–48 h after transfection, before G418 selection, after 2% PFA fixation and DAPI staining without recorded permeabilization. Field counts are technical sampling, not biological replication. The images do not establish plasma-membrane localization, and their batch relationship to P2 is unresolved.

The first numbered field is shown to make the endpoint readout inspectable without selecting the brightest field. Brightfield and DAPI provide cellular context; the GREEN and RED channels ask whether localized fluorescence accompanies the reporter fusion and independent mCherry marker.

![Or7a+ORCO field 01, brightfield and separate BLUE/GREEN/RED channels](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/aerosense-assets-20261017/225b1d2009d5-field-01-panel.webp)

*Or7a+ORCO, field 01, fixed-cell image panel. Display windows are BLUE 0–255, GREEN 0–120 and RED 0–180 digital values; brightfield retains exported levels. These display adjustments are not the quantitative input. The analysis uses the original channel TIFFs and the same blank-derived criteria across conditions. Compare the [untransfected field 01](https://static.igem.wiki/teams/6460/wiki/aerosense-assets-20261017/d7e6a0850fe4-field-01-panel.webp); the original 100 µm scale bars remain in the channel panels.*

| Blank-score cutoff | RED-positive objects | GREEN-positive objects |
|---|---:|---:|
| p95 | 45/192 (23.4%) | 18/192 (9.4%) |
| p99 | 21/192 (10.9%) | 3/192 (1.6%) |
| p99.5 | 20/192 (10.4%) | 3/192 (1.6%) |

*Counts across all available fields for this condition. p95, p99 and p99.5 are alternative blank-score cutoffs, not confidence levels or independent measurements. The denominator is unchanged across cutoffs.*

Most of the GREEN-positive count disappears between p95 and p99, while the three objects remaining at p99 also remain at p99.5. The RED marker is detectable in more eligible objects than the GREEN signal; the single dual-positive object does not establish a uniformly co-expressing culture.

BBa_26ZAGFK0__Or7a-IRES-mCherry.md.title: Interpretation and next validation for the Or7a condition
BBa_26ZAGFK0__Or7a-IRES-mCherry.md.body_markdown:
The most informative retained odorant well is F01 (2-heptanone): R = **+0.1835**, B = **+0.2141**, and D = **+0.1176**. Inspection of the two rounds explains why this is not simply an 18.35% ligand-evoked rise: the buffer-round change is −0.1637, while the test-round change is only +0.0198. The positive contrast remains after the untransfected reference, but part of its magnitude comes from the earlier decline. The fusion-only 2-heptanone well also has D = +0.1056, so the sign is not specific to the Or7a module.

VUAA1 gives R = −0.0549 and D = −0.0833 in A01, with buffer reference H01 at R = −0.0307. Together with the sparse GREEN-positive endpoint count, these records motivate separating expression of the fusion from tuning-receptor ligand selection. They do not establish a nonfunctional Or7a protein: the microscopy and P2 preparations are not batch-linked, and P2 does not contain a validated concentration-response series.

The collection provides the [shared calculation definitions and validation requirements](00_COLLECTION.md). The single-well contrasts on this page remain descriptive; they are not a significance test or a receptor-response classification.

### Published sequence and assembly check

Read-only Registry sequence check, 19 October 2026: **2,546 bp**. Detected sites among EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI, BsmBI and BbsI: **EcoRI×1; PstI×3; BsmBI×1; BbsI×3**. Both sequence orientations were examined; see the index for motifs and counting. This does not certify an assembly standard or verify the experimental clone.
